mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes SLK 200 or 230 Kompressor engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M111 engine for the SLK 200 or 230 Kompressor costs £2,000-£3,400 supply-only; a rebuilt M271 engine for the R171 SLK 200 Kompressor costs £2,400-£3,600 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity - supercharged engine work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of head gasket failure on a Mercedes SLK 200 or 230 Kompressor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Coolant loss, overheating, white smoke from the exhaust, and oil in the coolant are the classic warning signs on the M111 engine. The original Victor Reinz fibre head gasket can fail with age, particularly between cylinders 3 and 4.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes SLK 200 Kompressor (M271)?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign on the M271 engine. The timing chain can stretch over time, especially on earlier models, and the plastic timing chain guides can wear down.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes SLK 200 or 230 Kompressor engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M111 engine is widely regarded as very solid and reliable, with the head gasket being the main weakness. The M271 engine has a reputation for timing chain issues, but otherwise is a reliable powerplant.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes SLK 200 and 230 Kompressor engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M111 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. The M271 can achieve similar mileage but may require timing chain attention between 60,000-100,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes SLK 200 or 230 Kompressor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the SLK is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M111 costs £2,000-£3,400 - far less than replacing a £3,000-£12,000 vehicle. Classic SLK values remain strong for well-maintained examples, making engine replacement a worthwhile investment.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz SLK 200/230 Kompressor - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The SLK 200 Kompressor and SLK 230 Kompressor launched with the R170 generation in 1996, powered by the M111 2.0-litre and 2.3-litre supercharged four-cylinder engines - robust, characterful units that defined the SLK's sporty personality. In 2004, the R171 generation introduced the M271 1.8-litre supercharged engine for the SLK 200 Kompressor, offering improved power and efficiency while retaining the supercharged character that SLK owners loved. The 230 Kompressor badge was retired with the R170, making the R170 SLK 230 Kompressor a beloved classic among Mercedes enthusiasts.

milestones.description: M111.943, 2.0L supercharged four-cylinder, 192hp @ 5,300rpm (SLK 200 Kompressor, R170 launch)
M111.973, 2.3L supercharged four-cylinder, 193hp @ 5,300rpm (SLK 230 Kompressor, R170 launch)
2004 - M111.983, 2.3L supercharged four-cylinder, 197hp (SLK 230 Kompressor facelift, R170)

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz SLK 200/230 Kompressor Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The SLK 200 and 230 Kompressor's supercharged M111 and M271 engines are characterful and rewarding, but both have well-documented weaknesses that become more pronounced with age and mileage. The M111 is prone to head gasket failure and supercharger clutch wear, while the M271 is notorious for timing chain stretch and camshaft adjuster issues. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M111 Head Gasket Failure - The Classic Kompressor's Most Common Weakness
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes SLK 200 Kompressor, SLK 230 Kompressor (M111.943, M111.973, M111.983, 1996-2004)
problems.rootCause: The M111's original Victor Reinz fibre head gasket can degrade with age and heat cycling, causing coolant loss and overheating. If ignored, it can lead to engine seizure and catastrophic failure. The head gasket issue is considered the most significant weakness of the otherwise excellent M111 engine.

problems.h4: M111 Supercharger Clutch & Bearing Wear - The Kompressor's Signature Issue
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes SLK 200 Kompressor, SLK 230 Kompressor (M111.943, M111.973, M111.983, 1996-2004)
problems.rootCause: The M111's supercharger relies on a magnetic clutch and bearings to engage and disengage properly. Over time, the clutch can fail to engage, bearings can wear, and the supercharger can develop a grumbling noise. The K40 relay is a common electrical component that can cause supercharger engagement issues.

problems.group: M271 Timing Chain Stretch & Camshaft Adjuster Failure
problems.h4: M271 Timing Chain Stretch & Camshaft Adjuster Failure - The R171's Critical Weakness
problems.rootCause: The M271 engine is notorious for timing chain stretch and guide wear. The plastic timing chain guides can wear down, and the chain can stretch due to extended oil change intervals or low-quality oil. Camshaft adjuster sprocket wear and camshaft adjuster magnet failure are also common. The characteristic cold-start rattle is the earliest warning sign.

problems.h4: M111/M271 Oil Leaks & Supercharger Issues - The Kompressor's Age-Related Problems
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes SLK 200 Kompressor, SLK 230 Kompressor (M111, M271, 1996-2010)
problems.rootCause: Both M111 and M271 engines can suffer from oil leaks due to aging gaskets. Valve cover gaskets, spark plug well seals, and camshaft seals can degrade over time. Supercharger issues are common across both engine families, with the M111 suffering from clutch and bearing wear and the M271 from timing chain and adjuster issues.
